$comment: W18 probe scene matrix - the union-and-stack bed, and NOTHING else reads this file.
It runs through VITREA_SCENES into its own fixtures dir under
packages/calibration/results/2026-09-05-w18-union-contour/probe/, so the canonical
scenes.json and the frozen bed stay untouched (contract X10). Both backgrounds reuse
an existing kind: nothing rebuilds and no TCC re-grant is needed for the rasters.
What it is for. W18 separates the CSS tier's interior residual on a small box and on a
stacked scene into parts. That separation is web-side and needs no native reading at
all. This bed answers three different questions, for the record and for the renderer's
own charter rather than for this wave's fit: whether Apple's 44x44 capsule sits at its
120x44 capsule's level (the size law's input, natively); whether a spacing of 12
merges natively and what a merge does to the interior, which the canonical
toolbar-group's own comment asked and no capture has answered; and where the stack's
native level sits against both of vitrea's tiers.
Every scene is filed 'recorded'. W9's rule files a probe cell as recorded when it
duplicates frozen-bed geometry whose twin is holdout or floored - which covers
capsule-button, toolbar-group and glass-over-glass here. The two components that are
NOT twins (capsule-sm, toolbar-group-wide) are filed the same way rather than being
split into calibration and validation, because X10 forbids fitting anything to this
bed at all: a split that named a cell 'calibration' would declare a fit phase that
this wave has ruled out, and compare's 'recorded' set is opt-in twice over, which is
the custody these readings need.

checkerboard.$comment: Spec-mandated. Every cell edge is a step edge, so one capture yields many edge-spread samples for blur system identification.

photo.$comment: A deterministic multi-frequency colour field rather than a real photograph: it carries broadband detail and saturated hue transitions (what a photo contributes to a glass diff) with no licensed asset and no decode differences between the two renderers.

capsule-sm.$comment: ONE of the toolbar-group's three circles, alone. The bed has no lone small box: every existing capsule cell is the 120x44 control, and W18's separation is precisely whether a 44x44 box at the same span behaves like it. Natively this asks whether Apple's material reads its own size law off the span alone, as vitrea's does on both tiers.

capsule-button.$comment: The canonical control. Capsules are exact in vitrea's field family (S2), so this scene isolates material error from corner error.

toolbar-group.$comment: Three siblings inside one GlassEffectContainer / GlassGroup — the container-scoped sampling case. Spacing 12 is inside plausible merge distance, so this also shows whether the two implementations union proximity the same way.

toolbar-group-wide.$comment: The canonical three-up's members at a spacing past every merge threshold either implementation carries: vitrea's renderer separates at 16 (DEFAULT_GROUP_UNION) and its web scene builder floors the sampling merge at 24, and GlassEffectContainer(spacing: 40) is declared here so the native container is asked for the same thing. Against toolbar-group's spacing 12 this is the control that says what a merge does natively, which the canonical scene's own comment asked for and no capture has answered.

glass-over-glass.$comment: S1's mandated scene: an overlay-plane proxy necessarily samples the BASE plane's rendered output, so the overlay's material must be calibrated against an already-glassed backdrop, not raw content. Without this scene the overlay tier has no ground truth at all.

rest.$comment: No interaction. The probe carries no pressed cell: the wave's question is the resting interior.

profiles.$comment: The probe's one profile. 1x only: this machine's display presents at 1x and the canonical 2x fixtures were captured on a reconfigured display, so a 2x probe is a session the user opens (W18 Decision Log 1 q1(a)). The 2x separation is web-side and says so.
